title: Grade 9 Multi-Step Linear Equations
seo_title: Grade 9 Linear Equations Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 math worksheets on multi-step linear equations for the BC curriculum: variables on both sides, brackets, fractions and decimals, and word problems with phone plans and memberships. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Do the same thing to both sides: expand the brackets, collect the x-terms on one side, then the numbers on the other.
body_html:
Keep the equation balanced

An equation is like a level balance. You can add, subtract, multiply or divide, as long as you do the same thing to both sides. To solve a multi-step equation, follow the same order every time:

  1. Expand any brackets.
  2. Clear fractions or decimals (optional).
  3. Collect the x-terms on one side.
  4. Collect the numbers on the other side.
  5. Divide by the coefficient of x. Then check.
Example 1: variables on both sides

Solve 7x − 4 = 3x + 20.

Subtract 3x from both sides: 4x − 4 = 20. Add 4: 4x = 24. Divide by 4: x = 6. Check: 7 × 6 − 4 = 38 and 3 × 6 + 20 = 38 ✓.

Answer: x = 6

Brackets: multiply both terms

The number in front of the brackets multiplies every term inside. A minus sign in front belongs to that number, so it changes the sign of both terms.

Example 2: brackets

Solve 5 − 2(x − 3) = 1.

Expand: −2(x − 3) = −2x + 6, so 5 − 2x + 6 = 1. Simplify: 11 − 2x = 1. Subtract 11: −2x = −10. Divide by −2: x = 5. Check: 5 − 2(5 − 3) = 5 − 4 = 1 ✓.

Answer: x = 5

Fractions and decimals

Multiply every term on both sides by the lowest common denominator (LCD). The fractions disappear. With decimals, multiply every term by 10 or 100.

Example 3: fractions

Solve x2 + x3 = 10.

The LCD of 2 and 3 is 6. Multiply every term by 6: 3x + 2x = 60. So 5x = 60 and x = 12. Check: 12 ÷ 2 + 12 ÷ 3 = 6 + 4 = 10 ✓.

Answer: x = 12

Example 4: decimals

Solve 0.4x + 1.2 = 3.6.

Multiply every term by 10: 4x + 12 = 36. Subtract 12: 4x = 24. Divide by 4: x = 6. Check: 0.4 × 6 + 1.2 = 2.4 + 1.2 = 3.6 ✓.

Answer: x = 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3(x − 4) = 3x − 4Multiply both terms: 3x − 12
−2(x − 3) = −2x − 6−2 × (−3) = +6, so −2x + 6
9 − (x − 4) = 9 − x − 4The minus changes both signs: 9 − x + 4
7x + 4 = 3x + 24: add 3xSubtract 3x from both sides: 4x + 4 = 24
x2 + 3 = x5: 5x + 3 = 2xMultiply every term by 10, including 3: 5x + 30 = 2x
Checking in a changed equationAlways check in the original equation

faq.q: How do you solve multi-step linear equations in Grade 9?
faq.a: Expand any brackets, collect the x-terms on one side and the numbers on the other, then divide by the coefficient of x. For 7x − 4 = 3x + 20, subtract 3x (4x − 4 = 20), add 4 (4x = 24) and divide by 4 (x = 6).

faq.q: Are multi-step equations part of the BC Math 9 curriculum?
faq.a: Yes. The BC Mathematics 9 Patterning standard includes multi-step one-variable linear equations, with brackets, variables on both sides, fractions and decimals.

faq.q: How do you solve an equation with variables on both sides?
faq.a: Subtract the smaller x-term from both sides so x is on one side only. Then solve the two-step equation that is left and check your answer in the original equation.

faq.q: How do you solve linear equations with fractions?
faq.a: Multiply every term on both sides by the lowest common denominator. For x/2 + x/3 = 10, multiply by 6 to get 3x + 2x = 60, so x = 12.

items.q: A number x goes through this machine and comes out as −19. What is x?
items.e: Undo in reverse order: −19 + 7 = −12, then −12 ÷ 3 = −4. Check: 3 × (−4) − 7 = −12 − 7 = −19 ✓. Wrong answers: 4 comes from a sign error in the last step; −12 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

items.q: What is the best first step to solve 4x − 9 = 23?
c: Add 9 to the left side only
items.e: 4x − 9 means “multiply by 4, then subtract 9.” Undo the last step first: add 9 to both sides, so 4x = 32. Then divide by 4: x = 8. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other side too.

items.q: You subtract 5 from both sides of −6x + 5 = 29. Which equation do you get?
items.e: 29 − 5 = 24, and −6x stays the same, so −6x = 24. Then divide by −6: x = −4. Check: −6 × (−4) + 5 = 24 + 5 = 29 ✓.

Subtract 8 from both sides: 5x = 35. Divide both sides by 5: 35 ÷ 5 = 7. So x = 7. Check: 5 × 7 + 8 = 43 ✓. Wrong answers: −7 comes from a sign error in the last step; 35 comes from forgetting to divide by 5.

Add 13 to both sides: 2x = 8. Divide both sides by 2: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So x = 4. Check: 2 × 4 − 13 = −5 ✓. Wrong answers: −9 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 13 instead of adding it; −4 comes from a sign error in the last step; 8 comes from forgetting to divide by 2.

Subtract 4 from both sides: −3x = 21. Divide both sides by −3: 21 ÷ (−3) = −7. So x = −7. Check: −3 × (−7) + 4 = 25 ✓. Wrong answers: 7 comes from a sign error in the last step; 21 comes from forgetting to divide by −3.

Subtract 6 from both sides: x4 = −5. Multiply both sides by 4: (−5) × 4 = −20. So x = −20. Check: (−20) ÷ 4 + 6 = 1 ✓. Wrong answers: 28 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 6 instead of subtracting it; 20 comes from a sign error in the last step; −5 comes from forgetting to multiply by 4.

Subtract 7 from both sides: −2x = 12. Divide both sides by −2: 12 ÷ (−2) = −6. So x = −6. Check: 7 − 2 × (−6) = 19 ✓. Wrong answers: −13 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 7 instead of subtracting it; 6 comes from a sign error in the last step; 12 comes from forgetting to divide by −2.

Subtract 15 from both sides: 6x = −36. Divide both sides by 6: (−36) ÷ 6 = −6. So x = −6. Check: 6 × (−6) + 15 = −21 ✓. Wrong answers: −1 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 15 instead of subtracting it; 6 comes from a sign error in the last step; −36 comes from forgetting to divide by 6.

Add 8 to both sides: −5x = 35. Divide both sides by −5: 35 ÷ (−5) = −7. So x = −7. Check: −5 × (−7) − 8 = 27 ✓. Wrong answers: 7 comes from a sign error in the last step; 35 comes from forgetting to divide by −5.

Add 7 to both sides: x3 = 5. Multiply both sides by 3: 5 × 3 = 15. So x = 15. Check: 15 ÷ 3 − 7 = −2 ✓. Wrong answers: −27 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 7 instead of adding it; −15 comes from a sign error in the last step; 5 comes from forgetting to multiply by 3.

Add 4 to both sides: 9x = 54. Divide both sides by 9: 54 ÷ 9 = 6. So x = 6. Check: 9 × 6 − 4 = 50 ✓. Wrong answers: −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; 54 comes from forgetting to divide by 9.

Subtract 8 from both sides: −36 = 4x. Divide both sides by 4: (−36) ÷ 4 = −9. So x = −9. Check: 4 × (−9) + 8 = −28 ✓. Wrong answers: −5 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 8 instead of subtracting it; 9 comes from a sign error in the last step; −36 comes from forgetting to divide by 4.

Subtract 12 from both sides: −5x = −30. Divide both sides by −5: (−30) ÷ (−5) = 6. So x = 6. Check: 12 − 5 × 6 = −18 ✓. Wrong answers: −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; −30 comes from forgetting to divide by −5.

Subtract 3 from both sides: −x2 = 5. Multiply both sides by −2: 5 × (−2) = −10. So x = −10. Check: −(−10) ÷ 2 + 3 = 8 ✓. Wrong answers: −22 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 3 instead of subtracting it; 10 comes from a sign error in the last step; 5 comes from forgetting to multiply by −2.

Subtract 11 from both sides: 8x = −40. Divide both sides by 8: (−40) ÷ 8 = −5. So x = −5. Check: 8 × (−5) + 11 = −29 ✓. Wrong answers: 5 comes from a sign error in the last step; −40 comes from forgetting to divide by 8.

Add 6 to both sides: −7x = −42. Divide both sides by −7: (−42) ÷ (−7) = 6. So x = 6. Check: −7 × 6 − 6 = −48 ✓. Wrong answers: −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; −42 comes from forgetting to divide by −7.

Subtract 3 from both sides: 12 = −4x. Divide both sides by −4: 12 ÷ (−4) = −3. So x = −3. Check: 3 − 4 × (−3) = 15 ✓. Wrong answers: 3 comes from a sign error in the last step; 12 comes from forgetting to divide by −4.

Subtract 9 from both sides: x6 = −5. Multiply both sides by 6: (−5) × 6 = −30. So x = −30. Check: (−30) ÷ 6 + 9 = 4 ✓. Wrong answers: 78 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 9 instead of subtracting it; 30 comes from a sign error in the last step; −5 comes from forgetting to multiply by 6.

Subtract 14 from both sides: −9x = −54. Divide both sides by −9: (−54) ÷ (−9) = 6. So x = 6. Check: −9 × 6 + 14 = −40 ✓. Wrong answers: −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; −54 comes from forgetting to divide by −9.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, x. What is x?
items.e: The balance shows 5x + 3 = 2x + 18. Take 2 blocks off both pans: 3x + 3 = 18. Take 3 off both pans: 3x = 15. Share 15 among the 3 blocks: x = 5. Check: left side 5 × 5 + 3 = 28; right side 2 × 5 + 18 = 28 ✓. Wrong answers: 7 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 3 instead of subtracting it; 15 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, x. What is x?
items.e: The balance shows 4x + 2 = x + 17. Take one block off both pans: 3x + 2 = 17. Take 2 off both pans: 3x = 15. Share 15 among the 3 blocks: x = 5. Check: left side 4 × 5 + 2 = 22; right side 5 + 17 = 22 ✓. Wrong answers: 3 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 15 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

items.q: Which step gets the x-terms on one side of 7x + 4 = 3x + 24?
c: Subtract 3x from the right side only
items.e: Subtracting 3x from both sides keeps the equation balanced and leaves x on one side only: 4x + 4 = 24. Then 4x = 20 and x = 5. Check: 7 × 5 + 4 = 39 and 3 × 5 + 24 = 39 ✓.

items.q: You subtract 2x from both sides of 6x − 5 = 2x + 11. Which equation do you get?
items.e: 6x − 2x = 4x and 2x − 2x = 0, so 4x − 5 = 11. Subtracting from only one side breaks the balance; adding gives 8x. Next: 4x = 16, so x = 4.

Subtract 3x from both sides: 4x − 4 = 20. Add 4 to both sides: 4x = 24. Divide both sides by 4: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. So x = 6. Check: left side 7 × 6 − 4 = 38; right side 3 × 6 + 20 = 38 ✓. Wrong answers: 4 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 4 instead of adding it; −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; 24 comes from forgetting to divide by 4.

Subtract 4x from both sides: 5x + 2 = −23. Subtract 2 from both sides: 5x = −25. Divide both sides by 5: (−25) ÷ 5 = −5. So x = −5. Check: left side 9 × (−5) + 2 = −43; right side 4 × (−5) − 23 = −43 ✓. Wrong answers: 5 comes from a sign error in the last step; −25 comes from forgetting to divide by 5.

Subtract 2x from both sides: 4x − 7 = −31. Add 7 to both sides: 4x = −24. Divide both sides by 4: (−24) ÷ 4 = −6. So x = −6. Check: left side 6 × (−6) − 7 = −43; right side 2 × (−6) − 31 = −43 ✓. Wrong answers: −3 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 6 comes from a sign error in the last step; −24 comes from forgetting to divide by 4.

Add 3x to both sides: 8 = 4x − 12. Add 12 to both sides: 20 = 4x. Divide both sides by 4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. So x = 5. Check: left side −3 × 5 + 8 = −7; right side 5 − 12 = −7 ✓. Wrong answers: 10 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; −1 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 12 instead of adding it; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Subtract 2x from both sides: −9 = 3x + 6. Subtract 6 from both sides: −15 = 3x. Divide both sides by 3: (−15) ÷ 3 = −5. So x = −5. Check: left side 2 × (−5) − 9 = −19; right side 5 × (−5) + 6 = −19 ✓. Wrong answers: −1 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 6 instead of subtracting it; 5 comes from a sign error in the last step; −15 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

Add x to both sides: 12 = 3x + 3. Subtract 3 from both sides: 9 = 3x. Divide both sides by 3: 9 ÷ 3 = 3. So x = 3. Check: left side 12 − 3 = 9; right side 2 × 3 + 3 = 9 ✓. Wrong answers: −9 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 5 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 3 instead of subtracting it; −3 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Add 2x to both sides: 4 = 5x − 21. Add 21 to both sides: 25 = 5x. Divide both sides by 5: 25 ÷ 5 = 5. So x = 5. Check: left side 4 − 2 × 5 = −6; right side 3 × 5 − 21 = −6 ✓. Wrong answers: −25 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step; 25 comes from forgetting to divide by 5.

Subtract 3x from both sides: 5x + 5 = −25. Subtract 5 from both sides: 5x = −30. Divide both sides by 5: (−30) ÷ 5 = −6. So x = −6. Check: left side 8 × (−6) + 5 = −43; right side 3 × (−6) − 25 = −43 ✓. Wrong answers: −4 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 5 instead of subtracting it; 6 comes from a sign error in the last step; −30 comes from forgetting to divide by 5.

Simplify each side: 2x + 5 = 4x − 7. Subtract 2x from both sides: 5 = 2x − 7. Add 7 to both sides: 12 = 2x. Divide both sides by 2: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. So x = 6. Check: left side 3 × 6 + 5 − 6 = 17; right side 4 × 6 − 7 = 17 ✓. Wrong answers: −2 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; −1 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 7 instead of adding it; −6 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Subtract 4x from both sides: 6x − 3 = 27. Add 3 to both sides: 6x = 30. Divide both sides by 6: 30 ÷ 6 = 5. So x = 5. Check: left side 10 × 5 − 3 = 47; right side 4 × 5 + 27 = 47 ✓. Wrong answers: 4 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 3 instead of adding it; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step; 30 comes from forgetting to divide by 6.

Add 5x to both sides: 6 = 3x − 15. Add 15 to both sides: 21 = 3x. Divide both sides by 3: 21 ÷ 3 = 7. So x = 7. Check: left side −5 × 7 + 6 = −29; right side −2 × 7 − 15 = −29 ✓. Wrong answers: 3 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; −3 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 15 instead of adding it; −7 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Subtract 5x from both sides: 4 = 4x. Divide both sides by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1. So x = 1. Check: left side 5 × 1 + 4 = 9; right side 9 × 1 = 9 ✓. Wrong answers: −1 comes from a sign error in the last step; 4 comes from forgetting to divide by 4.

Add 2x to both sides: 3x + 18 = 0. Subtract 18 from both sides: 3x = −18. Divide both sides by 3: (−18) ÷ 3 = −6. So x = −6. Check: left side −6 + 18 = 12; right side −2 × (−6) = 12 ✓. Wrong answers: 18 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 6 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 18 instead of subtracting it; −18 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

Simplify each side: 5x + 7 = x − 13. Subtract x from both sides: 4x + 7 = −13. Subtract 7 from both sides: 4x = −20. Divide both sides by 4: (−20) ÷ 4 = −5. So x = −5. Check: left side 2 × (−5) + 7 + 3 × (−5) = −18; right side −5 − 13 = −18 ✓. Wrong answers: 5 comes from a sign error in the last step; −20 comes from forgetting to divide by 4.

Add 4x to both sides: 11 = 3x − 10. Add 10 to both sides: 21 = 3x. Divide both sides by 3: 21 ÷ 3 = 7. So x = 7. Check: left side 11 − 4 × 7 = −17; right side −7 − 10 = −17 ✓. Wrong answers: −7 comes from a sign error in the last step; 21 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

Add 2x to both sides: 8x − 8 = 24. Add 8 to both sides: 8x = 32. Divide both sides by 8: 32 ÷ 8 = 4. So x = 4. Check: left side 6 × 4 − 8 = 16; right side −2 × 4 + 24 = 16 ✓. Wrong answers: 8 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 2 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 8 instead of adding it; −4 comes from a sign error in the last step.
Multiply both terms inside the brackets by 3: 3 × x = 3x and 3 × (−4) = −12. 3x − 4 comes from multiplying only the first term.
Multiply both terms by −2: −2 × x = −2x and −2 × (−5) = +10. A negative times a negative is positive, so the answer is −2x + 10. −2x − 10 comes from a sign error.
The minus in front of the brackets multiplies both terms by −1: −(x − 4) = −x + 4. So 9 − x + 4 = 13 − x, which is −x + 13. −x + 5 comes from changing only the sign of x.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 3(x − 2) = 3x − 6. Simplify each side: 3x − 6 = 15. Add 6 to both sides: 3x = 21. Divide both sides by 3: 21 ÷ 3 = 7. So x = 7. Check: 3(7 − 2) = 15 ✓. Wrong answers: 3 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 6 instead of adding it; −7 comes from a sign error in the last step; 21 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 4(x + 5) = 4x + 20. Simplify each side: 4x + 20 = 8. Subtract 20 from both sides: 4x = −12. Divide both sides by 4: (−12) ÷ 4 = −3. So x = −3. Check: 4(−3 + 5) = 8 ✓. Wrong answers: 7 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 20 instead of subtracting it; 3 comes from a sign error in the last step; −12 comes from forgetting to divide by 4.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): −2(x − 3) = −2x + 6. Simplify each side: −2x + 6 = 14. Subtract 6 from both sides: −2x = 8. Divide both sides by −2: 8 ÷ (−2) = −4. So x = −4. Check: −2(−4 − 3) = 14 ✓. Wrong answers: −10 comes from a sign error when expanding with a negative multiplier; 4 comes from a sign error in the last step; 8 comes from forgetting to divide by −2.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 5(x + 1) = 5x + 5. Simplify each side: 5x + 5 = 3x + 17. Subtract 3x from both sides: 2x + 5 = 17. Subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 12. Divide both sides by 2: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. So x = 6. Check: left side 5(6 + 1) = 35; right side 3 × 6 + 17 = 35 ✓. Wrong answers: 8 comes from multiplying only the first term inside the brackets; 11 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 5 instead of subtracting it; −6 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 2(x − 4) = 2x − 8. Simplify each side: 2x − 8 = 4x + 6. Subtract 2x from both sides: −8 = 2x + 6. Subtract 6 from both sides: −14 = 2x. Divide both sides by 2: (−14) ÷ 2 = −7. So x = −7. Check: left side 2(−7 − 4) = −22; right side 4 × (−7) + 6 = −22 ✓. Wrong answers: −5 comes from multiplying only the first term inside the brackets; −1 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 6 instead of subtracting it; 7 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 6(x − 1) = 6x − 6. Simplify each side: 4x − 6 = 18. Add 6 to both sides: 4x = 24. Divide both sides by 4: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. So x = 6. Check: 6(6 − 1) − 2 × 6 = 18 ✓. Wrong answers: 3 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 6 instead of adding it; −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; 24 comes from forgetting to divide by 4.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): −2(x − 3) = −2x + 6. Simplify each side: −2x + 11 = 1. Subtract 11 from both sides: −2x = −10. Divide both sides by −2: (−10) ÷ (−2) = 5. So x = 5. Check: 5 − 2(5 − 3) = 1 ✓. Wrong answers: −1 comes from a sign error when expanding with a negative multiplier; −6 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 11 instead of subtracting it; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 2(x + 3) = 2x + 6; 3(x − 1) = 3x − 3. Simplify each side: 2x + 6 = 3x − 3. Subtract 2x from both sides: 6 = x − 3. Add 3 to both sides: 9 = x. So x = 9. Check: left side 2(9 + 3) = 24; right side 3(9 − 1) = 24 ✓. Wrong answers: 4 comes from multiplying only the first term inside the brackets; 3 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 3 instead of adding it; −9 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 4(x − 2) = 4x − 8; −(x + 1) = −x − 1. Simplify each side: 3x − 9 = 9. Add 9 to both sides: 3x = 18. Divide both sides by 3: 18 ÷ 3 = 6. So x = 6. Check: 4(6 − 2) − (6 + 1) = 9 ✓. Wrong answers: 4 comes from multiplying only the first term inside the brackets; −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; 18 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): −3(x + 2) = −3x − 6; 2(x − 8) = 2x − 16. Simplify each side: −3x − 6 = 2x − 16. Add 3x to both sides: −6 = 5x − 16. Add 16 to both sides: 10 = 5x. Divide both sides by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2. So x = 2. Check: left side −3(2 + 2) = −12; right side 2(2 − 8) = −12 ✓. Wrong answers: 10 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; −2 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): −3(x + 1) = −3x − 3. Simplify each side: −3x + 4 = −8. Subtract 4 from both sides: −3x = −12. Divide both sides by −3: (−12) ÷ (−3) = 4. So x = 4. Check: 7 − 3(4 + 1) = −8 ✓. Wrong answers: 6 comes from a sign error when expanding with a negative multiplier; −4 comes from a sign error in the last step; −12 comes from forgetting to divide by −3.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 2(3x − 1) = 6x − 2; 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8. Simplify each side: 6x − 2 = 4x + 8. Subtract 4x from both sides: 2x − 2 = 8. Add 2 to both sides: 2x = 10. Divide both sides by 2: 10 ÷ 2 = 5. So x = 5. Check: left side 2(3 × 5 − 1) = 28; right side 4(5 + 2) = 28 ✓. Wrong answers: 1 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 3 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 2 instead of adding it; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 5(x − 2) = 5x − 10; −3(x − 4) = −3x + 12. Simplify each side: 2x + 2 = 10. Subtract 2 from both sides: 2x = 8. Divide both sides by 2: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So x = 4. Check: 5(4 − 2) − 3(4 − 4) = 10 ✓. Wrong answers: 16 comes from a sign error when expanding with a negative multiplier; 6 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 2 instead of subtracting it; −4 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): −2(x + 1) = −2x − 2. Simplify each side: 8 = −2x − 2. Add 2 to both sides: 10 = −2x. Divide both sides by −2: 10 ÷ (−2) = −5. So x = −5. Check: −2(−5 + 1) = 8 ✓. Wrong answers: −3 comes from a sign error when expanding with a negative multiplier; 5 comes from a sign error in the last step; 10 comes from forgetting to divide by −2.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 3(x − 5) = 3x − 15. Simplify each side: 3x − 11 = x − 1. Subtract x from both sides: 2x − 11 = −1. Add 11 to both sides: 2x = 10. Divide both sides by 2: 10 ÷ 2 = 5. So x = 5. Check: left side 3(5 − 5) + 4 = 4; right side 5 − 1 = 4 ✓. Wrong answers: −6 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 11 instead of adding it; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step; 10 comes from forgetting to divide by 2.

items.q:
Harjot solved 4(x + 3) = 32:
Step 1: 4x + 3 = 32
Step 2: 4x = 29, so x = 7.25
Which step has a mistake?
items.e: Step 1 multiplies only x by 4. Both terms must be multiplied: 4x + 12 = 32. Then 4x = 20, so x = 5. Check: 4(5 + 3) = 4 × 8 = 32 ✓.

items.q:
Mei solved −3(x − 2) = 21:
Step 1: −3x + 6 = 21
Step 2: −3x = 15, so x = −5
Which step has a mistake?
items.e: Step 1: −3 × x = −3x and −3 × (−2) = +6. Step 2: subtract 6, then divide by −3. Both steps are right. Check: −3(−5 − 2) = −3 × (−7) = 21 ✓.

items.q: Multiply every term of 0.3x + 1.2 = 2.7 by 10. Which equation do you get?
items.e: 10 × 0.3x = 3x, 10 × 1.2 = 12 and 10 × 2.7 = 27. Every term must be multiplied. Then 3x = 15, so x = 5. Check: 0.3 × 5 + 1.2 = 2.7 ✓.

items.q: What is the best number to multiply every term of x4 + x6 = 5 by to clear the fractions?
items.e: Use the lowest common denominator (LCD) of 4 and 6, which is 12. 12 × x4 = 3x and 12 × x6 = 2x, so 3x + 2x = 60 and x = 12. 24 also works but gives bigger numbers; 10 (4 + 6) does not clear both fractions.

Subtract 1.2 from both sides: 0.4x = 2.4. Divide both sides by 0.4: 2.4 ÷ 0.4 = 6. So x = 6. Check: 0.4 × 6 + 1.2 = 3.6 ✓. Wrong answers: 12 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 1.2 instead of subtracting it; −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; 2.4 comes from forgetting to divide by 0.4.

Subtract 0.5x from both sides: x − 2 = 3. Add 2 to both sides: x = 5. Check: left side 1.5 × 5 − 2 = 5.5; right side 0.5 × 5 + 3 = 5.5 ✓. Wrong answers: 2.5 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 1 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 2 instead of adding it; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Subtract 3.5 from both sides: 0.2x = 1.2. Divide both sides by 0.2: 1.2 ÷ 0.2 = 6. So x = 6. Check: 0.2 × 6 + 3.5 = 4.7 ✓. Wrong answers: 41 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 3.5 instead of subtracting it; −6 comes from a sign error in the last step; 1.2 comes from forgetting to divide by 0.2.

Add 1.5 to both sides: 2.5x = 7.5. Divide both sides by 2.5: 7.5 ÷ 2.5 = 3. So x = 3. Check: 2.5 × 3 − 1.5 = 6 ✓. Wrong answers: 1.8 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 1.5 instead of adding it; −3 comes from a sign error in the last step; 7.5 comes from forgetting to divide by 2.5.

Subtract 0.4x from both sides: 0.8x + 0.8 = 4. Subtract 0.8 from both sides: 0.8x = 3.2. Divide both sides by 0.8: 3.2 ÷ 0.8 = 4. So x = 4. Check: left side 1.2 × 4 + 0.8 = 5.6; right side 0.4 × 4 + 4 = 5.6 ✓. Wrong answers: 2 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; 6 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 0.8 instead of subtracting it; −4 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 0.6(x − 5) = 0.6x − 3. Simplify each side: 0.6x − 3 = 1.8. Add 3 to both sides: 0.6x = 4.8. Divide both sides by 0.6: 4.8 ÷ 0.6 = 8. So x = 8. Check: 0.6(8 − 5) = 1.8 ✓. Wrong answers: −2 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 3 instead of adding it; −8 comes from a sign error in the last step; 4.8 comes from forgetting to divide by 0.6.

Subtract 3.2 from both sides: −0.4x = −1.6. Divide both sides by −0.4: (−1.6) ÷ (−0.4) = 4. So x = 4. Check: 3.2 − 0.4 × 4 = 1.6 ✓. Wrong answers: −12 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 3.2 instead of subtracting it; −4 comes from a sign error in the last step; −1.6 comes from forgetting to divide by −0.4.

Subtract 0.25x from both sides: 1.5 = 0.5x − 2.5. Add 2.5 to both sides: 4 = 0.5x. Divide both sides by 0.5: 4 ÷ 0.5 = 8. So x = 8. Check: left side 0.25 × 8 + 1.5 = 3.5; right side 0.75 × 8 − 2.5 = 3.5 ✓. Wrong answers: −4 comes from adding the x-terms instead of subtracting them; −2 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 2.5 instead of adding it; −8 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Subtract 1.3 from both sides: 2x = 4.8. Divide both sides by 2: 4.8 ÷ 2 = 2.4. So x = 2.4. Check: 2 × 2.4 + 1.3 = 6.1 ✓. Wrong answers: 3.7 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 1.3 instead of subtracting it; −2.4 comes from a sign error in the last step; 4.8 comes from forgetting to divide by 2.

items.q: Solve: x2 + x3 = 10
items.e: Multiply every term on both sides by 6 (the LCD of 2 and 3): 6 × x2 = 3x; 6 × x3 = 2x; 6 × 10 = 60. So 5x = 60. Divide both sides by 5: 60 ÷ 5 = 12. So x = 12. Check: 12 ÷ 2 + 12 ÷ 3 = 10 ✓. Wrong answers: 2 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 6, not the whole numbers; −12 comes from a sign error in the last step; 60 comes from forgetting to divide by 5.

Multiply every term on both sides by 3 (the denominator): 3 × 2x3 = 2x; 3 × 8 = 24. So 2x = 24. Divide both sides by 2: 24 ÷ 2 = 12. So x = 12. Check: 2 × 12 ÷ 3 = 8 ✓. Wrong answers: 4 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 3, not the whole numbers; −12 comes from a sign error in the last step; 24 comes from forgetting to divide by 2.

Multiply every term on both sides by 4 (the denominator): 4 × 3x4 = 3x; 4 × 2 = 8; 4 × 7 = 28. So 3x − 8 = 28. Add 8 to both sides: 3x = 36. Divide both sides by 3: 36 ÷ 3 = 12. So x = 12. Check: 3 × 12 ÷ 4 − 2 = 7 ✓. Wrong answers: 3 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 4, not the whole numbers; −12 comes from a sign error in the last step; 36 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

Multiply every term on both sides by 3 (the denominator): 3 × x + 43 = x + 4; 3 × 5 = 15. So x + 4 = 15. Subtract 4 from both sides: x = 11. Check: (11 + 4) ÷ 3 = 5 ✓. Wrong answers: 1 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 3, not the whole numbers; 3 comes from dividing only x by the denominator, not the whole top; 19 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 4 instead of subtracting it.

Multiply every term on both sides by 5 (the denominator): 5 × x − 25 = x − 2; 5 × 3 = 15. So x − 2 = 15. Add 2 to both sides: x = 17. Check: (17 − 2) ÷ 5 = 3 ✓. Wrong answers: 5 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 5, not the whole numbers; 25 comes from dividing only x by the denominator, not the whole top; 13 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 2 instead of adding it.

items.q: Solve: x3 − 1 = x4 + 1
items.e: Multiply every term on both sides by 12 (the LCD of 3 and 4): 12 × x3 = 4x; 12 × 1 = 12; 12 × x4 = 3x; 12 × 1 = 12. So 4x − 12 = 3x + 12. Subtract 3x from both sides: x − 12 = 12. Add 12 to both sides: x = 24. Check: left side 24 ÷ 3 − 1 = 7; right side 24 ÷ 4 + 1 = 7 ✓. Wrong answers: 2 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 12, not the whole numbers; −24 comes from a sign error in the last step.

items.q: Solve: x + 12 = x + 74
items.e: Multiply every term on both sides by 4 (the LCD of 2 and 4): 4 × x + 12 = 2x + 2; 4 × x + 74 = x + 7. So 2x + 2 = x + 7. Subtract x from both sides: x + 2 = 7. Subtract 2 from both sides: x = 5. Check: left side (5 + 1) ÷ 2 = 3; right side (5 + 7) ÷ 4 = 3 ✓. Wrong answers: 24 comes from dividing only x by the denominator, not the whole top; 9 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 2 instead of subtracting it; −5 comes from a sign error in the last step.

Multiply every term on both sides by 5 (the denominator): 5 × 2x5 = 2x; 5 × 1 = 5; 5 × 7 = 35. So 2x + 5 = 35. Subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 30. Divide both sides by 2: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. So x = 15. Check: 2 × 15 ÷ 5 + 1 = 7 ✓. Wrong answers: 3 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 5, not the whole numbers; 20 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 5 instead of subtracting it; −15 comes from a sign error in the last step.

items.q: Solve: x2 − 3 = x5
items.e: Multiply every term on both sides by 10 (the LCD of 2 and 5): 10 × x2 = 5x; 10 × 3 = 30; 10 × x5 = 2x. So 5x − 30 = 2x. Subtract 2x from both sides: 3x − 30 = 0. Add 30 to both sides: 3x = 30. Divide both sides by 3: 30 ÷ 3 = 10. So x = 10. Check: left side 10 ÷ 2 − 3 = 2; right side 10 ÷ 5 = 2 ✓. Wrong answers: 1 comes from multiplying only the fractions by 10, not the whole numbers; −10 comes from using the wrong inverse: subtracting 30 instead of adding it; 30 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

sets.title: Word problems: phone plans, memberships and more

items.q: Phone plan A costs $30 a month plus $5 for each GB of data. Plan B costs $45 a month plus $2 for each GB. For how many GB do the two plans cost the same?
items.e: Let g be the number of GB. Set the two costs equal: 30 + 5g = 45 + 2g. Subtract 2g from both sides: 3g + 30 = 45. Subtract 30 from both sides: 3g = 15. Divide both sides by 3: 15 ÷ 3 = 5. So g = 5. Check: left side 30 + 5 × 5 = 55; right side 45 + 2 × 5 = 55 ✓. Both plans cost $55. Wrong answers: 15 GB comes from forgetting to divide by 3; 25 GB comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 30 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Phone A costs $300 up front plus $40 a month. Phone B costs nothing up front but $65 a month. After how many months is the total cost the same?
items.e: Let m be the number of months: 300 + 40m = 65m. Subtract 40m from both sides: 300 = 25m. Divide both sides by 25: 300 ÷ 25 = 12. So m = 12. Check: left side 300 + 40 × 12 = 780; right side 65 × 12 = 780 ✓. Both phones cost $780. Wrong answers: 25 months comes from giving the difference in the monthly cost, $65 − $40; 300 months comes from forgetting to divide by 25.

items.q: A community centre in Surrey charges $8 for each drop-in swim. A membership costs $40 plus $3 a swim. For how many swims do both options cost the same?
items.e: Let v be the number of swims: 40 + 3v = 8v. Subtract 3v from both sides: 40 = 5v. Divide both sides by 5: 40 ÷ 5 = 8. So v = 8. Check: left side 40 + 3 × 8 = 64; right side 8 × 8 = 64 ✓. Both cost $64. Wrong answers: 5 swims comes from dividing 40 by 8 and ignoring the $3 a swim; 40 swims comes from forgetting to divide by 5.

items.q: A climbing gym in Squamish charges $15 a visit, or $90 for a membership plus $6 a visit. For how many visits do both options cost the same?
items.e: Let v be the number of visits: 15v = 90 + 6v. Subtract 6v from both sides: 9v = 90. Divide both sides by 9: 90 ÷ 9 = 10. So v = 10. Check: left side 15 × 10 = 150; right side 90 + 6 × 10 = 150 ✓. Both cost $150. Wrong answers: 6 visits comes from dividing 90 by 15 and ignoring the $6 a visit; 90 visits comes from forgetting to divide by 9.

items.q: Gym A charges a $60 sign-up fee plus $25 a month. Gym B charges $40 a month and no sign-up fee. After how many months is the total cost the same?
items.e: Let m be the number of months: 60 + 25m = 40m. Subtract 25m from both sides: 60 = 15m. Divide both sides by 15: 60 ÷ 15 = 4. So m = 4. Check: left side 60 + 25 × 4 = 160; right side 40 × 4 = 160 ✓. Both cost $160. Wrong answers: 15 months comes from giving the difference in the monthly cost, $40 − $25; 60 months comes from forgetting to divide by 15.

items.q: Phone plan A costs $25 a month plus $4 for each GB of data. Plan B costs $40 a month plus $1 for each GB. Which equation finds the number of GB, g, when the plans cost the same?
items.e: Each plan costs its monthly fee plus its price per GB times g: 25 + 4g and 40 + g. Set them equal. Solve: 3g = 15, so g = 5 GB. Check: 25 + 20 = 45 and 40 + 5 = 45 ✓.

items.q: A ski hill near Kelowna sells day tickets for $85. A season pass costs $480 plus $25 for each day. After how many days does the season pass cost the same as day tickets?
items.e: Let d be the number of days: 85d = 480 + 25d. Subtract 25d from both sides: 60d = 480. Divide both sides by 60: 480 ÷ 60 = 8. So d = 8. Check: left side 85 × 8 = 680; right side 480 + 25 × 8 = 680 ✓. Both cost $680. Wrong answers: 60 days comes from giving the difference in the daily cost, $85 − $25; 480 days comes from forgetting to divide by 60.

items.q: Sofia has $150 saved and adds $20 each week. Simran has $310 and spends $20 each week. After how many weeks will they have the same amount?
items.e: Let w be the number of weeks: 150 + 20w = 310 − 20w. Add 20w to both sides: 40w + 150 = 310. Subtract 150 from both sides: 40w = 160. Divide both sides by 40: 160 ÷ 40 = 4. So w = 4. Check: left side 150 + 20 × 4 = 230; right side 310 − 20 × 4 = 230 ✓. They both have $230. Wrong answers: 8 weeks comes from using 20w − 20w = 0 instead of adding: 160 ÷ 20; 160 weeks comes from forgetting to divide by 40.

items.q: Tank A holds 500 L of water and drains 15 L a minute. Tank B holds 200 L and fills 10 L a minute. After how many minutes do the tanks hold the same amount?
items.e: Let t be the number of minutes: 500 − 15t = 200 + 10t. Add 15t to both sides: 500 = 25t + 200. Subtract 200 from both sides: 300 = 25t. Divide both sides by 25: 300 ÷ 25 = 12. So t = 12. Check: left side 500 − 15 × 12 = 320; right side 200 + 10 × 12 = 320 ✓. Both tanks hold 320 L. Wrong answers: 60 minutes comes from subtracting 10t instead of adding 15t (300 ÷ 5); 28 minutes comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 200 instead of subtracting it; 300 minutes comes from forgetting to divide by 25.

items.q: For a fundraiser, a Grade 9 class pays $120 to set up a T-shirt printer plus $4 for each shirt. They sell each shirt for $10. How many shirts must they sell to break even?
items.e: Let s be the number of shirts. Break even means money in = money out: 10s = 120 + 4s. Subtract 4s from both sides: 6s = 120. Divide both sides by 6: 120 ÷ 6 = 20. So s = 20. Check: left side 10 × 20 = 200; right side 120 + 4 × 20 = 200 ✓. Wrong answers: 12 shirts comes from dividing 120 by 10 and ignoring the $4 cost; 30 shirts comes from dividing 120 by 4; 120 shirts comes from forgetting to divide by 6.

items.q: Owen is choosing a summer job in the Okanagan. Job A pays $18 an hour. Job B pays $16 an hour plus a $40 bonus each week. For how many hours a week do the jobs pay the same?
items.e: Let h be the number of hours: 18h = 16h + 40. Subtract 16h from both sides: 2h = 40. Divide both sides by 2: 40 ÷ 2 = 20. So h = 20. Check: left side 18 × 20 = 360; right side 16 × 20 + 40 = 360 ✓. Both jobs pay $360. Wrong answers: 40 hours comes from forgetting to divide by 2.

items.q: The sum of three consecutive whole numbers is 141. What is the smallest number?
items.e: Let n be the smallest number. The numbers are n, n + 1 and n + 2: n + n + 1 + n + 2 = 141. Simplify each side: 3n + 3 = 141. Subtract 3 from both sides: 3n = 138. Divide both sides by 3: 138 ÷ 3 = 46. So n = 46. Check: 46 + 46 + 1 + 46 + 2 = 141 ✓. The numbers are 46, 47 and 48. Wrong answers: 47 comes from giving the middle number; 48 comes from giving the largest number; 138 comes from forgetting to divide by 3.

items.q: A rectangular garden is 3 m longer than twice its width. Its perimeter is 54 m. How wide is it?
items.e: Let w be the width. The length is 2w + 3, and the perimeter is 2 × length + 2 × width: 2(2w + 3) + 2w = 54. Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 2(2w + 3) = 4w + 6. Simplify each side: 6w + 6 = 54. Subtract 6 from both sides: 6w = 48. Divide both sides by 6: 48 ÷ 6 = 8. So w = 8. Check: 2(2 × 8 + 3) + 2 × 8 = 54 ✓. The garden is 8 m wide and 19 m long. Wrong answers: 9 m comes from using only one width in the perimeter (2(2w + 3) + w = 54); 19 m comes from giving the length, not the width; 10 m comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 6 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Ji-woo’s aunt is 3 times as old as Ji-woo. In 12 years, she will be twice as old as Ji-woo. How old is Ji-woo now?
items.e: Let a be Ji-woo’s age now. In 12 years, Ji-woo is a + 12 and the aunt is 3a + 12: 3a + 12 = 2(a + 12). Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 2(a + 12) = 2a + 24. Simplify each side: 3a + 12 = 2a + 24. Subtract 2a from both sides: a + 12 = 24. Subtract 12 from both sides: a = 12. Check: left side 3 × 12 + 12 = 48; right side 2(12 + 12) = 48 ✓. Wrong answers: 36 years old comes from giving the aunt’s age.

items.q: Four friends each buy a movie ticket and an $8 snack combo. They pay $96 in total. How much is one ticket?
items.e: Let t be the price of one ticket: 4(t + 8) = 96. Expand the brackets (multiply both terms inside): 4(t + 8) = 4t + 32. Simplify each side: 4t + 32 = 96. Subtract 32 from both sides: 4t = 64. Divide both sides by 4: 64 ÷ 4 = 16. So t = 16. Check: 4(16 + 8) = 96 ✓. Wrong answers: $24 comes from dividing 96 by 4 and forgetting the snack; $22 comes from multiplying only t by 4 (4t + 8 = 96); $32 comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 32 instead of subtracting it.

items.q: Bike rental A charges $12 plus $8 an hour. Bike rental B charges $20 plus $6 an hour. For how many hours do they cost the same?
items.e: Let h be the number of hours: 12 + 8h = 20 + 6h. Subtract 6h from both sides: 2h + 12 = 20. Subtract 12 from both sides: 2h = 8. Divide both sides by 2: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So h = 4. Check: left side 12 + 8 × 4 = 44; right side 20 + 6 × 4 = 44 ✓. Both cost $44. Wrong answers: 16 hours comes from using the wrong inverse: adding 12 instead of subtracting it; 8 hours comes from forgetting to divide by 2.

items.q: A community centre in Burnaby charges $9 for each yoga class, or $50 for a membership plus $4 a class. Which equation finds the number of classes, c, when both options cost the same?
items.e: Drop-in: 9 for each class, so 9c. Membership: 50 plus 4 for each class, so 50 + 4c. Set them equal. Solve: 5c = 50, so c = 10 classes. Check: 9 × 10 = 90 and 50 + 40 = 90 ✓.

items.q: A bike share in Vancouver has two plans. Plan A costs $1.50 to unlock plus $0.30 a minute. Plan B costs $0.40 a minute with no unlock fee. For how many minutes do the plans cost the same?
items.e: Let m be the number of minutes: 1.5 + 0.3m = 0.4m. Subtract 0.3m from both sides: 1.5 = 0.1m. Divide both sides by 0.1: 1.5 ÷ 0.1 = 15. So m = 15. Check: left side 1.5 + 0.3 × 15 = 6; right side 0.4 × 15 = 6 ✓. Both cost $6.00. Wrong answers: 150 minutes comes from misplacing the decimal point; 5 minutes comes from dividing 1.50 by 0.30.

items.q: A trip to Science World costs a school $250 for the bus plus $9 for each student. A tour company offers $14 a student with the bus included. For how many students do the options cost the same?
items.e: Let s be the number of students: 250 + 9s = 14s. Subtract 9s from both sides: 250 = 5s. Divide both sides by 5: 250 ÷ 5 = 50. So s = 50. Check: left side 250 + 9 × 50 = 700; right side 14 × 50 = 700 ✓. Both cost $700. Wrong answers: 5 students comes from giving the difference in the cost per student, $14 − $9; 250 students comes from forgetting to divide by 5.

items.q: A hockey team gets 2 points for a win and 1 point for a tie. This season the team has 4 ties and 38 points. How many games has the team won?
items.e: Let w be the number of wins: 2w + 4 = 38. Subtract 4 from both sides: 2w = 34. Divide both sides by 2: 34 ÷ 2 = 17. So w = 17. Check: 2 × 17 + 4 = 38 ✓. Wrong answers: 19 wins comes from forgetting to subtract the 4 tie points; 21 wins comes from adding the 4 tie points; 34 wins comes from forgetting to divide by 2.
